preconditions.description: Attacker must be the owner of the contract
The contract must hold at least one NFT token (any ERC721) that belongs to it

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call withdrawNft() function with parameters: token_ = address of the NFT contract, destination_ = attacker's address, tokenId_ = ID of the NFT to steal. This will transfer any NFT held by the contract to the attacker's address without any restrictions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The Withdrawable contract has a withdrawNft() function that is only protected by the onlyOwner modifier. This allows the contract owner to transfer any NFT from the contract's balance to any address without restrictions. The function calls IERC721(token_).transferFrom(address(this), destination_, tokenId_), which will succeed as long as the contract holds the NFT or has approval to transfer it.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call withdrawNft() to steal an NFT that the contract holds. We'll need to first ensure the contract actually holds an NFT by deploying a mock ERC721 and minting it to the contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner of the CUSD contract. 2. Deploy a mock ERC721 token. 3. Mint an NFT (tokenId = 1) to the CUSD contract address. 4. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 5. Call withdrawNft() on the CUSD contract with the mock ERC721 address, attacker address, and tokenId = 1. 6. Verify the NFT was transferred to the attacker.
